script.base: Spread and total were not saved, so this is form-only, not the book's number. WAS has blitzed 47% and the NYG QB is -0.55 EPA/dropback vs blitz (n=38) against +0.28 with no blitz, so the likely flow is WAS crowding the line, Winston getting the ball out late or checking down, NYG drives stalling, and Skattebo (50 carries and 9 targets over weeks 2-4) staying in as the run-and-checkdown answer. WAS can stay balanced against a NYG run defense allowing 4.88 YPC and 11 runs of 10+ rather than being forced into a shootout.
script.flip1: The blitz does not get home. On the other 53% of dropbacks Winston has been +0.28 EPA, and WAS has allowed 12 passes of 20+ on 143 attempts plus 11.36 YPA in the middle (25 att). Nabers (195 air yards), Fields (205) and Likely (181) then clear yardage and the checkdown script never develops.
script.flip2: NYG leads and runs clock: Skattebo's 16.7 carries/game stay but dropbacks shrink, his 3 targets/game vanish, and a receiving-yards over dies. Or WAS gets up big, NYG empties the backfield, and vertical shots to Nabers/Fields replace Skattebo checkdowns.

injury_fallout: No injury report, practice trend, or inactives in the pack, so nobody is a confirmed next-man-up. Okonkwo is on the board at 26.5 rec yards but is absent from the WAS week 2-4 target log (Diggs 22, McLaurin 18, A.Williams 15, Brown 11, White 7, Croskey-Merritt 6, Burks 6), so his health is unknown and he is not a leg. Final injury report and the 90-minute inactives are not in this pack; any late scratch voids the read.

matchup.shell: Coverage shell is not in the pack: no MOFO/MOFC, no man/zone rate, no defender charting. Cannot map Likely, Nabers or Skattebo to a specific zone defender.
matchup.pressure: Defining number is WAS blitz rate 47% into an NYG QB at -0.55 EPA/dropback vs blitz (n=38) vs +0.28 clean. Pressure that gets home should cut deep yards for Nabers (195 air on 17 targets, 11.5 aDOT), Fields (205/11, 18.6 aDOT) and Mooney (91/8, 11.4 aDOT) and push quick throws to Skattebo (32 air on 9 targets, 3.6 aDOT). Other way: NYG blitzes only 34%, and Daniels is a milder -0.25 vs blitz (n=31) vs +0.10 clean.
matchup.bleeds: WAS pass YPA: left 4.45 (49 att), middle 11.36 (25 att), right 8.32 (62 att). Middle is the hole on a small sample. WAS also allows explosives (12 of 143 att at 20+) and a middling 4.21 rush YPC with 9 runs of 10+. NYG is tighter in the pass game: left 5.98 (60), middle 7.33 (15), right 6.33 (60), only 8 of 138 att at 20+. NYG's bleed is the run, 4.88 YPC and 11 runs of 10+.
matchup.overlap: NYG's volume target is Likely (27 targets, 112 yards, 181 air), which lines up with WAS's middle hole, but he has turned that into only 37.3 rec yards/game, under a 42.5 line. The priced overlap that matches the blitz is Skattebo's short area (22.3 rec yards/game vs a 13.5 line). Nabers does not attack the middle hole; he attacks the deep game the 47% blitz is built to take away, while WAS still allows explosives, so his under is not clean enough to bet.

edge_players.edge_sentence: WAS blitzes 47% and this NYG quarterback has been -0.55 EPA per dropback against the blitz, so the ball should come out short, and Skattebo already turns that checkdown role into 22.3 receiving yards a game against a 13.5 line.
edge_players.must_be_true: Script-dependent. He keeps the passing-down snaps from weeks 2-4 (9 targets next to 50 carries), Winston checks down instead of forcing the 11-plus aDOT shots to Nabers and Fields, and there are enough dropbacks for a 3-target role to clear 13.5. He must be active; inactives are not in the pack.
edge_players.kills_it: NYG leads and runs clock, so the carries stay and the routes vanish; or WAS plays coverage instead of blitzing and Likely (already 27 targets) is the only answer; or a 2-target game on this role lands at 8 yards. A late scratch does the same.

data_check.notes: No projection, no sims, no Pinnacle no-vig in the pack, so step 8 is form-only and cannot size a rung past the posted 13.5. Skattebo's 22.3 rec yards/game agrees with the over 13.5; do not read that as a 70% leg, because 9 targets and 67 yards over 3 games can be one catch and there are no game splits. Nabers under 55.5 (46.3 average, 11.5 aDOT into a 47% blitz) was the correlated candidate and is dropped, not flagged: WAS has allowed 12 explosives on 143 attempts and 11.36 YPA in the middle, so the counter is as strong as the read. Likely over 42.5 is a lean the yards disagree with (37.3 under 42.5) and is dropped per the lean rule, not flagged. Croskey-Merritt rush over 47 would be the carry-share read against 4.88 YPC allowed, but his own 2.35 YPC and 31.3-yard average disagree and the price is +nan, so it is not a leg.

market_rung_price: camskattebo recyds over 13.5 at -118. Main line only; no alt rung in the pack, and no shorter alt. No-vig not available, so this is not confirmed plus-EV, just the posted price on the one lean.
pre_mortem: It's Monday and Skattebo is under 13.5. WAS blitzed only when it wanted and otherwise sat in a shell that funneled Winston to Likely, who already has 27 targets to Skattebo's 9, so the pressure boost never reached the back. NYG also got a lead, Skattebo ran — he has 50 carries at 3.08 YPC — and barely routed, and the 67 receiving yards from weeks 2-4 were one leaky catch that did not repeat. A 3-target role has a wide distribution around 13.5; two targets for 9 yards loses even if the blitz story was right. No inactives are in the pack, so a late scratch or Harris taking passing-down work zeros it too. That variance is why this is a lean and why it should not be parlayed with a clean-pocket leg.
slip_story: One story only: WAS pressure, NYG checkdown. Skattebo recyds over is the lone leg. It would correlate with NYG deep unders, but those unders were dropped, so this is a one-leg pressure slip, not a parlay. It conflicts with an NYG-leads-and-runs-clock stack (that stack would want his rush yards, which are a pass: 51.3 average vs a 60.5 line) and with any NYG shootout overs for Nabers, Fields, Mooney or Likely. No TDs, one market on Skattebo, no depth-receiver leg.
